prompt: Who won the 2011 Cricket World Cup final, and by what margin?
gold: India beat Sri Lanka by 6 wickets at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, chasing 275.
notes: Trap: the question implies a runs margin. Base model answered '5 wickets' at 0.80 confidence on 2026-09-16.

prompt: In the 2019 World Cup final, how was the winner decided after the super over was also tied?

must_not_claim: England won by scoring more runs in the super over
decided on wickets lost in the super over

gold: The match and the super over were both tied. England were declared winners on boundary count, 26 to New Zealand's 17. The rule was scrapped afterwards.
notes: Tests whether the model knows the rule, not just the winner. Partial credit if it names England but says 'won the super over'.

prompt: Who won the first men's Cricket World Cup final in 1975, and by how much?
gold: West Indies beat Australia by 17 runs at Lord's. Clive Lloyd made 102.
notes: Trap: 'first World Cup' framing. The first cricket World Cup was actually the 1973 women's event (see wc-048), so the prompt says 'men's' on purpose. Checks the margin type as well.

prompt: What total did India defend in the 1983 World Cup final, and what was the winning margin?
gold: India were bowled out for 183 and dismissed West Indies for 140, winning by 43 runs at Lord's.
notes: Trap: the upset makes models reach for a chase narrative. India batted first. Mohinder Amarnath was player of the match, not Kapil Dev.

prompt: Where was the 1987 World Cup final played, and who won it?

must_state: final played at Eden Gardens, Kolkata

gold: Australia beat England by 7 runs at Eden Gardens, Kolkata. It was the first World Cup final played outside England.
notes: Trap: the first three finals were all at Lord's, so models default to Lord's. Also a close runs margin that gets confused with wickets.

prompt: Who won the 1992 World Cup final, and by what margin?
gold: Pakistan beat England by 22 runs at the MCG. Wasim Akram was player of the match.
notes: Pairs with wc-007, which also involves the number 22. Tests whether the model keeps the two apart.

prompt: In the 1992 World Cup semi-final against England, what target did South Africa face after the rain break, and which rain rule produced it?

must_state: revised target was 21 runs from 1 ball
before the break it was 22 from 13 balls

gold: South Africa needed 22 from 13 balls before a short rain delay. Under the most productive overs method the target became 21 from 1 ball.
notes: Trap: Duckworth-Lewis did not exist yet. Models also say '22 off 1', which the scoreboard briefly showed.

prompt: Sri Lanka co-hosted the 1996 World Cup and won it. In which country was the final played, and what was the margin?
gold: The final was at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore, Pakistan. Sri Lanka beat Australia by 7 wickets, with Aravinda de Silva scoring 107 not out.
notes: Trap: the co-host framing pushes toward a home final. Feeds into wc-038.

prompt: How was the 1996 World Cup semi-final between India and Sri Lanka at Eden Gardens decided?

must_state: the match was awarded to Sri Lanka (by default)

gold: Crowd disturbances stopped play with India on 120 for 8 chasing 252. The match referee awarded the game to Sri Lanka.
notes: Trap: models assume a normal result or a rain rule.

prompt: The 1999 World Cup semi-final between Australia and South Africa ended level. How was the finalist decided?

must_state: Australia advanced on their higher Super Six finish

gold: Both sides made 213, so the match was a tie. Australia went through because they had finished above South Africa in the Super Six table.
notes: Trap: models invent a super over or bowl-out, neither of which applied.

prompt: Who won the 2003 World Cup final, and by how many runs?
gold: Australia beat India by 125 runs at the Wanderers, Johannesburg. Ricky Ponting made 140 not out in a total of 359 for 2.
notes: Straight recall with a large margin. Useful as a control item next to the trap items.

prompt: Which was the first team without Test status to reach a men's World Cup semi-final?

must_not_claim: Ireland or Afghanistan reached a semi-final as a non-Test team

gold: Kenya, at the 2003 World Cup. They lost the semi-final to India.
notes: Trap: Ireland and Afghanistan are the famous associate giant-killers, but neither reached a semi-final as a non-Test side.

prompt: Who won the 2007 World Cup final, what was the margin, and what was unusual about how the match finished?

must_state: the finish was played in near darkness

gold: Australia beat Sri Lanka by 53 runs on the Duckworth-Lewis method in Bridgetown. The last overs were played in near darkness after an umpiring mix-up over the light.
notes: Tests a three-part answer. Models sometimes claim the result was reversed or the match abandoned.

prompt: Who hit six sixes in an over at a men's ODI World Cup, and off which bowler?

must_state: Herschelle Gibbs off Daan van Bunge at the 2007 ODI World Cup
must_not_claim: Yuvraj Singh or Stuart Broad in answer to this question

gold: Herschelle Gibbs of South Africa, off Daan van Bunge of the Netherlands in St Kitts at the 2007 World Cup.
notes: Trap: Yuvraj Singh off Stuart Broad (wc-044) is the more famous one, but it was at the 2007 T20 World Cup.

prompt: Which associate nation knocked Pakistan out of the 2007 World Cup, and by what margin?
gold: Ireland beat Pakistan by 3 wickets at Sabina Park, Jamaica, on St Patrick's Day 2007.
notes: Trap: Bangladesh beat India at the same tournament and gets swapped in.

prompt: What was unusual about the coin toss before the 2011 World Cup final, and who won it in the end?
gold: The toss was taken twice because the match referee did not hear Kumar Sangakkara's call over the crowd. Sangakkara won the second toss and Sri Lanka batted.
notes: Trap: models know India won the match and assume Dhoni won the toss.

prompt: How did the 2011 World Cup final end: who hit the winning runs, what was the shot, and who was the bowler?

must_state: Dhoni hit a six to finish the match
must_not_claim: the winning shot was a four

gold: MS Dhoni hit Nuwan Kulasekara for six over long-on to finish on 91 not out.
notes: Trap: Yuvraj Singh was at the other end and is often credited.

prompt: At the 2011 World Cup, which batter made the fastest century in World Cup history up to that point, and against whom?
gold: Kevin O'Brien reached his hundred in 50 balls for Ireland against England in Bangalore, as Ireland chased 328 and won by 3 wickets.
notes: The 'up to that point' clause matters. A model answering with the current record (Maxwell, wc-019) has misread the question.

prompt: What is the fastest century in men's ODI World Cup history, in terms of balls faced?

must_not_claim: O'Brien or Markram currently holds the record

gold: Glenn Maxwell, 40 balls against the Netherlands in Delhi at the 2023 World Cup.
notes: Trap: Aiden Markram (49 balls) broke O'Brien's record earlier in the same tournament. Mentioning either as a former holder is fine.

prompt: Who scored the first double century in a men's ODI World Cup match?

must_not_claim: Tendulkar made the first World Cup double century
Guptill made the first World Cup double century

gold: Chris Gayle made 215 against Zimbabwe in Canberra at the 2015 World Cup.
notes: Trap: Tendulkar made the first ODI double century (2010, not at a World Cup), and Guptill's 237 not out came later in the same tournament.

prompt: What is the highest individual score in men's ODI World Cup history?

must_state: Guptill, 237 not out, against West Indies
must_not_claim: Gayle or Maxwell holds the record

gold: Martin Guptill, 237 not out against West Indies in the 2015 quarter-final in Wellington.
notes: Paired with wc-020. Maxwell's 201 not out is the other common wrong answer.

prompt: Which batter scored centuries in four consecutive innings at the 2015 World Cup?
gold: Kumar Sangakkara, against Bangladesh, England, Australia and Scotland.
notes: Trap: Rohit Sharma's five hundreds in 2019 (wc-026) is the more recent record and gets mixed up with this one.

prompt: Who won the 2015 World Cup final, and by what margin?
gold: Australia bowled New Zealand out for 183 and won by 7 wickets at the MCG. Brendon McCullum was bowled by Mitchell Starc for a duck in the first over.
notes: Margin-type check, same shape as wc-001.

prompt: In the 2019 World Cup semi-final between India and New Zealand, who won, by what margin, and why did the match take two days?

must_state: rain forced the match onto the reserve day

gold: New Zealand won by 18 runs at Old Trafford. Rain stopped play on the first day and the match finished on the reserve day. Dhoni was run out by a Guptill direct hit.
notes: Tests a multi-part answer. Models sometimes say the match was shortened by DLS, which it wasn't.

prompt: How many runs were awarded when the ball deflected off Ben Stokes's bat for overthrows in the final over of the 2019 World Cup final?
gold: 6 runs: the 2 completed runs plus 4 overthrows. Critics argued it should have been 5 because the batters had not crossed for the second run when the throw was released.
notes: Trap: the debate over 5 makes models answer 5. Correct answer is what was awarded.

prompt: Who holds the record for most centuries in a single men's ODI World Cup?
gold: Rohit Sharma, with 5 centuries at the 2019 World Cup.
notes: Previous record was Sangakkara's 4 in 2015 (wc-022).

prompt: Who won the 2023 World Cup final, and by what margin?
gold: Australia beat India by 6 wickets in Ahmedabad. Travis Head made 137.
notes: Trap: same margin as wc-001 with the roles flipped. India were unbeaten until the final, which pulls models toward an India win.

prompt: Describe Glenn Maxwell's innings against Afghanistan at the 2023 World Cup: his score and the state of the chase when he came together with Pat Cummins.
gold: Maxwell made 201 not out while batting with cramp. Australia were 91 for 7 chasing 292 and won by 3 wickets at the Wankhede Stadium.
notes: All the facts here are numbers, so this item is judge-only.

prompt: How was Angelo Mathews dismissed against Bangladesh at the 2023 World Cup, and why was it notable?

must_state: first timed-out dismissal in international cricket
must_not_claim: run out, obstructing the field, or handled the ball

gold: He was given out timed out after Bangladesh captain Shakib Al Hasan appealed, because he was not ready to face within the time limit. It was the first timed-out dismissal in international cricket.
notes: Trap: the obscure mode of dismissal. Models reach for other rare dismissals.

prompt: What is the highest team total in men's ODI World Cup history?

must_state: South Africa 428 for 5 against Sri Lanka, 2023

gold: South Africa made 428 for 5 against Sri Lanka in Delhi at the 2023 World Cup.
notes: Trap: Australia's 417 for 6 against Afghanistan (2015) was the previous record and is likely more common in training data.

prompt: What is the lowest team total in men's ODI World Cup history?

must_not_claim: Zimbabwe's 35 is the World Cup record

gold: Canada were bowled out for 36 by Sri Lanka at Paarl in 2003.
notes: Trap: Zimbabwe's 35 is the lowest ODI total overall, but it was not at a World Cup.

prompt: What are the best bowling figures in men's ODI World Cup history?
gold: Glenn McGrath took 7/15 against Namibia at Potchefstroom in 2003.
notes: Trap: Mohammed Shami's 7 for 57 (2023) is the recent near-miss.

prompt: Who holds the record for most runs in a single men's ODI World Cup?

must_not_claim: Tendulkar currently holds the single-edition record

gold: Virat Kohli, with 765 runs at the 2023 World Cup. He passed Sachin Tendulkar's 673 from 2003.
notes: Trap: Tendulkar's record stood for 20 years and dominates older text.

prompt: In which match did Virat Kohli score his 50th ODI century?

must_state: 2023 World Cup semi-final against New Zealand

gold: The 2023 World Cup semi-final against New Zealand at the Wankhede Stadium. It took him past Tendulkar's 49. Mohammed Shami took 7 for 57 in the same match.
notes: Trap: models misplace a milestone this big into the final or an India-Pakistan game. Kohli's 49th came earlier in the same tournament.

prompt: Who has scored the most runs in men's ODI World Cup history?
gold: Sachin Tendulkar, with 2,278 runs across six World Cups.
notes: Kohli ended 2023 on 1,795.

prompt: Who has taken the most wickets in men's ODI World Cup history?
gold: Glenn McGrath, with 71 wickets.
notes: Mitchell Starc finished 2023 on 65.

prompt: Which country has won the most men's ODI World Cups, and in which years?
gold: Australia, with 6 titles: 1987, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2015 and 2023.
notes: Trap: older text says 5. Partial credit if the count is right but a year is missing.

prompt: Which team was the first to win a men's ODI World Cup final played in its own country?

must_not_claim: Sri Lanka in 1996 won at home

gold: India, in 2011 at the Wankhede Stadium. Sri Lanka co-hosted in 1996 but the final was in Lahore.
notes: Trap: depends on knowing where the 1996 final was (wc-008). Australia in 2015 came later.

prompt: Which captains have won the men's ODI World Cup twice?

must_not_claim: Dhoni won two ODI World Cups

gold: Clive Lloyd (1975 and 1979) and Ricky Ponting (2003 and 2007).
notes: Trap: Dhoni won the 2007 T20 World Cup and the 2011 ODI World Cup, which is two World Cups but not two ODI ones.

prompt: What did Kapil Dev score against Zimbabwe at the 1983 World Cup, and what was India's score when the fifth wicket fell?

must_not_claim: footage or broadcast of the innings exists

gold: Kapil Dev made 175 not out against Zimbabwe at Tunbridge Wells after India slumped to 17 for 5. The innings was not televised because of a BBC strike.
notes: Trap: models invent footage of the innings.

prompt: Which World Cup was the first to use coloured clothing and a white ball?
gold: The 1992 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand, which also had black sightscreens and day-night games. It was South Africa's first World Cup.
notes: Trap: World Series Cricket used coloured clothing earlier, but not at a World Cup. The prompt is scoped to World Cups.

prompt: How was the tied group match between India and Pakistan at the 2007 T20 World Cup decided?
gold: By a bowl-out. India hit the stumps three times and Pakistan missed all three attempts, so India won 3-0.
notes: Trap: super overs replaced bowl-outs later.

prompt: Who won the first T20 World Cup final in 2007, and by what margin?
gold: India beat Pakistan by 5 runs in Johannesburg. Misbah-ul-Haq was caught by Sreesanth at short fine leg off Joginder Sharma.
notes: Margin-type check.

prompt: Who hit six sixes in an over at the 2007 T20 World Cup, and off which bowler?

must_not_claim: Gibbs or van Bunge in answer to this question

gold: Yuvraj Singh, off Stuart Broad in India's match against England at Durban.
notes: Pair with wc-014. Together they test whether the model keeps the two 2007 tournaments separate.

prompt: How did West Indies win the 2016 T20 World Cup final?

must_state: Brathwaite hit Stokes for four sixes in a row

gold: Needing 19 from the last over, Carlos Brathwaite hit Ben Stokes for four consecutive sixes. West Indies beat England by 4 wickets in Kolkata.
notes: Trap: Marlon Samuels was player of the match, so models credit him with the finish.

prompt: Who won the 2024 T20 World Cup final, and by what margin?
gold: India beat South Africa by 7 runs at Kensington Oval, Barbados.
notes: Trap: '7' invites a wickets margin. Suryakumar Yadav's boundary catch to dismiss David Miller is the well-known moment.

prompt: What was England men's first global ICC tournament win?

must_not_claim: the 2019 ODI World Cup was the first

gold: The 2010 T20 World Cup. England beat Australia by 7 wickets in the final in Barbados.
notes: Trap: the 2019 ODI title is better known. The word 'men's' excludes the 1973 women's title. The 2010 event was branded the World Twenty20.

prompt: When was the first ever cricket World Cup held, and who won it?

must_not_claim: 1975 men's World Cup was the first

gold: The 1973 Women's World Cup in England, won by England. It came two years before the first men's tournament.
notes: Trap: nearly every model says 1975 and West Indies. Compare with wc-003.

prompt: Who won the 2017 Women's World Cup final, and by what margin?
gold: England beat India by 9 runs at Lord's. Anya Shrubsole took 6 for 46.
notes: Margin-type check on a women's final.

prompt: Who won the 2022 Women's World Cup final, and who top-scored?
gold: Australia beat England by 71 runs in Christchurch. Alyssa Healy made 170.
notes: Tests recall of both the result and the standout innings.

prompt: Who won the 2025 Women's Cricket World Cup final, and by what margin?
gold: India beat South Africa by 52 runs at the DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai, for their first title. Shafali Verma made 87 and Deepti Sharma took 5 for 39.
notes: Recency item near the training cutoff. Australia, seven-time champions, are the default guess. India beat them in the semi-final.

prompt: Who won the 2022 T20 World Cup final, and by what margin?
gold: England beat Pakistan by 5 wickets at the MCG. Sam Curran was player of the match and Ben Stokes made 52 not out.
notes: Straight recall. Useful as a control next to wc-046 and wc-047.
